ds: Borrowers finance the same receivable or goods more than once, forge invoices, or obtain advances on fictitious trade. Fraud may involve connected parties and weak verification of underlying transactions.

src.t: FATF and Egmont Group, Trade-Based Money Laundering: Trends and Developments (2020)

ind.n: Same invoice or bill of lading presented to multiple financiers
ind.cx: Duplicate financing detected by registry or internal matching.
ind.ds: The same invoice, bill of lading or goods are presented to multiple financiers or invoiced more than once.
ind.cn: Same invoice or shipment financed or invoiced multiple times

ind.n: Invoices from related parties with round values
ind.cx: Counterparties share ownership and amounts look artificial.
ind.ds: Counterparties share ownership and amounts look artificial.

ind.n: Debtor denies or cannot confirm the invoice
Repayments funded by new financing from same borrower
ind.cx: Revolving structure where old invoices are settled with new drawings.
ind.ds: Revolving structure where old invoices are settled with new drawings.

ind.n: Shipping documents inconsistent with goods or route
ind.cx: Dates, weights, ports or vessel details do not align.
ind.ds: Bill of lading, invoice, customs, letter of credit or payment details disagree on goods, quantity, price, origin, parties or route.
ind.cn: Trade documents inconsistent with each other

ind.n: Sudden growth in financed volume without business rationale
ind.cx: Facility usage rises faster than turnover.
ind.ds: Facility usage rises faster than turnover.

ind.cx: Proceeds sent to parties outside the trade.
ind.ds: Proceeds sent to parties outside the trade.

ind.n: Borrower reluctant to allow inspection or direct debtor contact

ctl.ds: Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.

ctl.n: Duplicate document and duplicate financing detection
ctl.ds: Hashes and fuzzy-matches invoice and shipping documents within and across clients and checks shared registries so one asset cannot be financed twice. It detects reused and fabricated paper.

Confirms the existence of underlying goods, services or receivables directly with the obligor or through inspection before funds are advanced. It defeats fictitious invoices and transactions that exist only on paper.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.
Verifies instructions, detail changes and unusual requests by contacting the customer on a channel held on file, never one supplied in the request. It defeats impersonation and account takeover.

ctl.n: Sampling, quality assurance and analytics audit
ctl.ds: Takes periodic samples of customer files, alert decisions, relied-upon files or analytical datasets and tests them for exceptions, duplicates and errors, feeding findings back to owners and training. It independently confirms that controls work as designed.

Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

Checks identity and supporting documents for tampering, forgery, template reuse and internal inconsistency, and corroborates their data against authoritative or reliable independent sources. It exposes altered or counterfeit credentials that pass a visual check.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.
